35d59810.task:
Target: local codebase at /workspace/adgrid (a React/Vite web app "adgrid" - digital-signage ad marketplace - with a Supabase backend: ~190 SQL migrations under supabase/migrations/ implementing RLS policies, and ~44 Deno edge functions under supabase/functions/*/index.ts plus shared business-logic modules under supabase/functions/_shared/*.ts, many of which already have *.test.js unit tests). There is also a mobile/ (Expo) app and packages/core.

IMPORTANT SCOPE NOTE: only the local code at /workspace/adgrid is authorized. The .env file references a live hosted Supabase project (https://hkqiuwnppxkkztacwicj.supabase.co) - DO NOT send any network requests to that hosted domain or any other external host; it is out of scope. All validation must stay local (reading code, running local unit tests via `npm test`/vitest, running standalone Node/Python scripts against exported pure functions, static analysis tools). No supabase CLI/deno/docker are installed in this sandbox, so do not attempt to spin up a local Supabase stack - focus on static + local-unit-test analysis.

Your job is PURE MAPPING/TRIAGE, not deep exploitation - you are laying groundwork for other specialized agents. Do the following:

1. Complete the source-aware static baseline bundle per the source_aware_sast skill: semgrep has already been run once (results at /workspace/adgrid/.source-aware/semgrep.json) - review it briefly, then add an ast-grep (sg) structural pass scoped to supabase/functions and src/ (build sg-targets.txt from semgrep scope), a secrets pass (gitleaks and/or trufflehog) across the whole repo, and a trivy fs pass (vuln,misconfig) across the repo. Store artifacts under /workspace/adgrid/.source-aware/.
2. Build an architecture/threat map and save it as a `wiki` category note (use create_note) covering:
   - Auth model: how Supabase auth/JWT is used, user roles (advertiser/operator/admin/screen), how role checks are enforced (RLS vs edge function code vs frontend-only)
   - Full inventory of supabase/functions/*/index.ts: one line each describing purpose, what auth check it performs (service-role key usage, JWT verification, ownership checks), and any request body it trusts
   - RLS policy summary: which tables have RLS, notable history of "fix"/"harden"/"lock" migrations (there are many - e.g. harden_new_user_role, lock_bookings_update, revoke_anon_bookings_update, fix_profiles_update_check, rls_and_function_hardening, campaign_hierarchy_rls, marketplace exclusivity fixes) - flag any table/policy that still looks permissive or inconsistent
   - Business-logic modules in supabase/functions/_shared/ (pacing, dayparting, creativeSelection, transferReversal, makegood, approvalSla, shareToken, ruleEvaluator, scanQuality, cronGuard, requestSize) - summarize what invariant each is supposed to enforce
   - Payment/Stripe flow: charge-campaign, stripe-webhook, stripe-capture-payment, stripe-refund, stripe-create-intent, stripe-billing, trigger-payout, operator-billing, create-connect-account, confirm-connect-account, manage-payment-method, get-stripe-charges - map the money flow and where trust boundaries are
   - Invite/token flows: create-screen-invite, accept-screen-invite, accept-operator-invite, invite-operator, invite-team-member, handle-approval-token, mark-screen-invite-booked, record-screen-invite-view, shareToken.ts - note token generation/validation logic and expiry/scoping
   - Frontend routes/views under src/views/* (admin, advertiser, operator, display, invite, public) and how they call supabase (src/lib) - flag any obvious client-trust issues (e.g. relying on client-side role checks only)
   - A ranked top-15 list of the highest-risk candidate issues you noticed (file:line references) across IDOR/BFLA, SQLi, business logic, race conditions, auth bypass, SSRF - for other specialist agents to pick up. Do NOT file vulnerability reports yourself - just document candidates with enough detail (file, line, why suspicious) for a validation agent to act on.

Also run `npm test` (vitest) once to confirm the existing unit test suite passes/fails as a sanity baseline, and note any failing tests that might hint at logic bugs.

When done, reply with a summary and the note id(s) you created.

35b166c8.task:
Target: local codebase at /workspace/adgrid. Perform a supply-chain / SCA scan following the dependency_cve_scanning skill.

Scope:
- Root package.json + pnpm-lock.yaml (React/Vite web app)
- packages/core/package.json (workspace package)
- mobile/package.json (Expo/React Native app), if present, and its lockfile
- Deno third-party imports referenced in supabase/functions/**/index.ts and supabase/functions/_shared/*.ts (esm.sh / deno.land / npm: specifiers) - check versions pinned in import statements against known CVEs

For each dependency with a matching published CVE affecting the installed/pinned version, verify the CVE ID and version range (web_search if needed), do a lightweight reachability check (is the package imported/used in app code vs just a transitive dev dependency), and file it with create_dependency_report - one report per CVE x package. Do NOT use create_vulnerability_report for these (no dynamic PoC needed for known-CVE dependency findings). Do not silently skip a finding because reachability is unclear - just set the reachability level honestly (e.g. "unknown" or "not_imported") and still file it if the CVE/version match is confirmed.

Do not test against any live/hosted network endpoints - this is a pure static/manifest-based scan. When finished, report back a summary of what was filed (or confirmation that no exploitable known-CVE dependencies were found).
